author: WP15
summary: Alpha.1-era networking chapter: session types, SystemLink/ENet transport, discovery, migration, delivery mapping, compatibility quirks, the shared async action and lifetime hardening. Several claims are stale at TARGET: maxGamers is forwarded (not 69), PlayerMatch/Ranked/JoinInvited are refused, ReadColor is fixed, opcode 0x07 exists and LocalWithLeaderboards adds no persistence. Tutorial 97 and the net internals page covered most mechanics; the wire and discovery protocol tables, trust model, delivery table, properties-indexer quirk, web topology and the hardening history now live on a new deep dive.

concepts.text: The Net surface combines one functional LAN route with compatibility lifecycles: SystemLink uses the vendored ENet transport, the other session types do not, and code that only observes session objects can miss the difference.
tokens: cannot tell a real session from a simulated one

concepts.text: SystemLink provides ENet host/join, LAN discovery, handshake, application-data relay, disconnect handling, simulated latency/loss and host migration.
A Local session has synthetic state and events but no transport and no data delivery, not even to its own gamers.

concepts.text: Claim that PlayerMatch and Ranked are stubs: at the snapshot Create and Find refuse them with GamerServicesNotAvailableException because they need a matchmaking service.

Session factories hand back caller-owned objects: Create and Join return a raw NetworkSession* (Find returns a collection by value, JoinInvited never returns); Dispose releases transport and owned gamers but does not delete the object, so the caller does both, the destructor disposing as a fallback.

concepts.text: ENetBackend uses a star topology: clients send application data to the host, which relays it to the target peer.
NetworkGamer::Id and IsHost are consistent across machines because the host assigns wire ids, unlike FNA's fixed 0/true placeholders.
Claim that RoundtripTime reads ENet's peer measurement: it does, but only for directly connected peers, so only the host's view of its clients is measured and every other gamer stays at zero.
tokens: the host's view of its clients only

concepts.text: LAN discovery uses UDP port 61190, protocol version 1 and a 150 ms search window; the finder sends broadcast plus loopback queries and de-duplicates replies by connect port.
The game session uses an OS-assigned ENet port on native hosts; Emscripten requests the fixed port 61191 and cannot perform raw-UDP browser discovery.
QualityOfService from discovery reports the measured query-to-reply round-trip time; bandwidth remains unmeasured.
Claimed opcode table ClientHello 0x01, ServerWelcome 0x02, join/leave 0x03/0x04, reserved 0x05, state change 0x06, app data 0x10: at the snapshot there is also SessionPropertiesBroadcast 0x07.
The ENet host has two channels and at most 31 peers.

Up to 64 application sends may wait for handshake completion and the 65th evicts the oldest; disconnect, gamer removal and migration purge affected entries; an internal dropped-packet counter is not public API.
Discovery packets are version-checked before parsing and advertised property indices must lie in [0, 256), rejecting negative indices and a huge index that would drive billions of Add calls.
One-byte list counts on the session wire refuse to encode more than 255 entries instead of wrapping.
A peer that repeats ClientHello after completing its handshake is disconnected, and host-only broadcasts from a non-host peer are rejected with a disconnect.
tokens: A repeated hello disconnects the peer.

concepts.text: The checks assume an untrusted client can reproduce the documented wire format; there is no authentication or encryption.
tokens: There is no authentication or encryption on either wire

concepts.text: With AllowHostMigration false, losing the host ends the session; when true, survivors choose the lowest remaining wire id from their shared roster with no election packet, the owner promotes itself and the others rediscover its cached gamertag and reconnect, retrying discovery three times.

Migration clears remote gamers and wire-id state first, so reconnecting peers see leave and join events and new NetworkGamer objects; sockets and object identity are not preserved and the session ends if the new host cannot be found.
SimulatedLatency and SimulatedPacketLoss affect received application data only, not session-management packets or the host's relay hop; FNA stores them without applying them.
ENet expresses three behaviours for XNA's five SendDataOptions: None unsequenced, InOrder plain sequenced, Reliable/ReliableInOrder/Chat reliable and ordered.

ENet's reliable channel is ordered, so 'reliable but unordered' cannot be reproduced without another protocol; Reliable receives the stronger ordered guarantee and Chat uses the same route by CNA policy.
Even in SystemLink, voice and invitations are absent: EnableSendVoice and SendPartyInvites do nothing and the voice and private-slot properties keep false defaults.
NetworkMachine::RemoveFromSession() throws NotImplementedException.
Invite and TrueSkill/arbitration events are never raised.

Claim that JoinInvited creates a synthetic PlayerMatch lifecycle: at the snapshot BeginJoinInvited always throws GamerServicesNotAvailableException and EndJoinInvited rejects every result with ArgumentException.
concepts.note: Not copied; the page states the refusal and why EndJoinInvited cannot bypass it.

concepts.text: Historical: PacketWriter wrote Color as four bytes while PacketReader::ReadColor read four floats, so the two were not inverses.
concepts.note: Fixed at TARGET: ReadColor reads four bytes (source comment explains the old 16-byte read); the page tells it as history and notes cross-revision incompatibility.

concepts.text: ReceiveData(PacketReader&, NetworkGamer*&) fills and rewinds the reader but returns 0 because its local length is never updated (an FNA quirk kept); gate reads with IsDataAvailable or use the byte-vector overload for an accurate count.

The mutable NetworkSessionProperties indexer grows the collection on an out-of-range access because C++ cannot tell read from write through the proxy; it appends one slot at the end (not up to the index); use a const reference or getItem for bounds-checked reads and setItem for XNA's setter.

All session Begin*/End* pairs share one static NetworkSessionAction*, and a second Begin* throws while it is set; at the snapshot Begin* also refuses while a session is alive, so one operation and one session per process.

concepts.text: The current Dispose is idempotent, clears every gamer collection and Host and releases owned gamers; AddressSanitizer, not ordinary unit success, exposed the original double-dispose, so lifetime changes need sanitizer runs.
Codec, hostile-input, policy, ownership, simulated loss/latency and compatibility behaviours have focused tests.

An out-of-process, two-instance ENet harness establishes cross-process SystemLink delivery on the tested host; it does not establish Internet matchmaking, voice, browser UDP discovery or untested platforms.

issues.text: Local and LocalWithLeaderboards sessions deliver no packets at all, not even between local gamers; PlayerMatch/Ranked/JoinInvited are refused.

ReceiveData(PacketReader&) writes the packet at position 0 of the reader's stream without truncating it, so reusing one PacketReader for a shorter packet after a longer one appears to leave stale trailing bytes and an old Length (depends on sharp-runtime MemoryStream::Write, read at a sibling revision).
issues.evidence: modules/net/src/Xna/LocalNetworkGamer.cpp (ReceiveData PacketReader overload); sharp-runtime (sibling, not pinned) MemoryStream::Write

issues.text: NetworkSessionAction reports CompletedSynchronously == false although it is completed before Begin* returns.
A joining machine's session is constructed with MaxSupportedGamers (31) and four private slots (FNA FIXME placeholders), so a client's MaxGamers/PrivateGamerSlots do not mirror the host's.
Voice (EnableSendVoice, SendPartyInvites), NetworkMachine::RemoveFromSession, arbitration/TrueSkill events and QualityOfService bandwidth are unimplemented.
On Emscripten, LAN discovery is a no-op, hosting is only meaningful for a Node.js relay (fixed port 61191), and Join returns before the handshake.

Process-spawning transport and dispatcher tests are compiled out on Windows, Emscripten, Android and iOS; multi-machine discovery/migration, Windows shared-port binding and browser paths have no test evidence.
The non-const NetworkSessionProperties indexer appends a slot on any out-of-range access (documented, accepted divergence; const access and getItem are strict).
